articles.author: dorian-pike
articles.title: Lynch brings Mt. Silver back, and Blackthorn never gets the last possession
articles.dek: Garshawn Lynch rushes for 145 yards and two touchdowns as the Reds reverse a 14–7 deficit, win 21–14 and earn a conference-title rematch with Saffron.

body.text: Garshawn Lynch had seventeen carries to make his argument. By the time Mt. Silver finished its final possession, Blackthorn had no remaining opportunity to answer it. The Reds won 21–14, recovered from a seven-point third-quarter deficit and advanced to host Saffron in the Kanto–Johto championship. Lynch supplied 145 rushing yards, two touchdowns and the recurring problem that kept the Dragons’ defense on the field while Hatterene waited on the sideline.

I was the only member of our five-writer panel to pick Mt. Silver this week. I mention that because four colleagues are currently preparing explanations of considerable length. The Reds had lost the regular-season meeting 30–22, their quarterback injuries were real, and Blackthorn had just scored five passing touchdowns at Cinnabar. Those were sound reasons to expect a difficult afternoon. Mt. Silver supplied one for itself, then found the players and possessions required to survive it.

The comeback belonged to more than the leading runner. Crem Ftzpatrik completed eighteen of twenty-five passes for 195 yards without an interception. Prinplup caught all four of his targets, including the third-down completion that sustained the winning touchdown drive. Scep Smith Jr. caught the deciding score after losing a fumble before halftime. The defense kept Blackthorn from converting two early recoveries into points and forced the final punt that allowed Lynch and Rat Grange to close the game.
Two lost fumbles and a manageable deficit

Mt. Silver reached halftime down 7–0 despite moving the ball into two possessions that ended in lost fumbles. Gregar Jenings caught a twenty-five-yard pass before fumbling to Blastoise at 3:54 of the second quarter. Later, Scep Smith Jr. lost the ball after a six-yard completion, with Politoed recovering. Blackthorn finished both ensuing possessions with punts. That is a substantial defensive contribution in a game decided by one touchdown.

Connor McLarren had plenty to discuss during the interval. His offense had punted twice before the turnovers, and Blayz Matthews’s two first-quarter sacks had not kept Blackthorn scoreless. Hatterene found Ninjask for a twenty-eight-yard touchdown at 4:59 of the second quarter. The Dragons had a lead, an efficient scoring receiver and the possibility of starting the second half with the ball. Mt. Silver still had a game it could rescue because the defense had limited the damage around those mistakes.

There is a temptation to describe every close playoff win as an exhibition of composure. The first half gives that description some limits. The Reds repeatedly surrendered possessions they had already moved forward. Blackthorn deserves credit for creating and recovering those fumbles, and Mt. Silver deserves credit for the subsequent stops. Both teams had something tangible to regret when they walked off at halftime.
We gave them the ball twice and still had a seven-point game. I suggested we try keeping it for a while. Garshawn seemed to enjoy that part of the discussion.

body.text: The kickoff changes the available field

body.text: The second half began with Blackthorn’s Ninjask returning the kickoff twenty-five yards to the Dragons’ twenty-six and fumbling. Cranidos recovered for Mt. Silver. In a game with no interceptions, that special-teams turnover gave the home offense its shortest touchdown opportunity and changed the immediate pressure on both sidelines.

Lynch finished the resulting three-play, twenty-six-yard drive with an eight-yard run to the right. The touchdown arrived at 5:15, and Weepinbell’s extra point tied the game. Mt. Silver had needed almost an entire half to reach the scoreboard; it needed less than a minute after the break to erase the deficit. The recovery created the chance, and Lynch converted it into the outcome the Reds had failed to secure on longer first-half possessions.

Blackthorn answered with its best drive of the half. Hatterene led a seven-play, eighty-two-yard possession and found Ninjask deep left for a forty-three-yard touchdown at 3:26. The receiver finished with four catches for 112 yards and both Dragons touchdowns. His return fumble was costly, and his offensive production was essential. A useful account of his afternoon includes both rather than asking one play to explain every snap he took.

The Dragons led 14–7. Their quarterback had thrown two touchdowns without an interception, and the explosive play had restored the lead quickly enough to quiet the home comeback. Mt. Silver’s next response would require a full drive. This time there was no short field from a turnover waiting to simplify the assignment.
Lynch supplies the second response

The Reds traveled sixty-eight yards in six plays. Lynch’s eighteen-yard run on second-and-ten moved them into immediate scoring position; his seven-yard run up the middle finished the possession at 1:51. He had now scored on consecutive Mt. Silver drives, first from a short field and then from a conventional one. Those two circumstances matter because they demonstrate how the rushing production supported the comeback beyond the opening recovery.

Lynch averaged 8.5 yards on his seventeen carries, with a longest run of eighteen. The total came through repeated productive attempts rather than one enormous escape surrounded by losses. Rat Grange added forty yards on seven carries. Together they gave Ftzpatrik a practical way to keep the offense moving without requiring the available quarterback to imitate Hatterene’s previous five-touchdown performance.

Blackthorn’s next possession lasted seven plays and gained eighteen yards before a punt. Mt. Silver took over with thirty-eight seconds remaining in the third quarter. From there the Reds assembled the seventy-one-yard drive that decided the game, mixing their established rushing advantage with timely completions to receivers whose names had appeared less prominently in the pregame argument.

Ftzpatrik opened the fourth quarter with a twenty-four-yard completion to Doduo. Lynch followed with ten rushing yards. Two incompletions then produced third-and-ten, the sort of down on which a narrow game can return to balance. Prinplup caught a fourteen-yard pass to the right. His next reception gained eight, leaving second-and-one. Ftzpatrik found Scep Smith Jr. over the short middle for the one-yard touchdown at 4:32.

body.text: The final 3:18 belongs to Mt. Silver

Blackthorn had one possession after falling behind. It gained twenty-seven yards in five plays, then punted with 3:18 remaining. The decision placed the next burden on the Dragons’ defense: stop the run, recover the ball and give Hatterene another chance to tie. Mt. Silver instead held possession through the final whistle.

The closing drive covered forty-seven yards in nine recorded plays. Rat Grange gained six yards on consecutive runs around the two-minute warning. Lynch then gained six and seven, moving the chains again before Ftzpatrik’s kneels. The Reds did not need another score. They needed first downs, and the two runners supplied them against a defense that understood precisely what a failed stop would cost.

Mt. Silver finished with twenty first downs to Blackthorn’s ten and 182 rushing yards to the Dragons’ sixty-three. The Reds converted four of six third downs; Blackthorn converted three of eight. Hatterene’s 219 passing yards and two touchdowns kept the visitors competitive, but his offense punted five times. Grovyle, perfect on nine targets at Cinnabar, caught three of eight for eighteen yards here. The previous week’s receiving success offered no automatic solution against a different defense.
Another home game, with a thinner receiving group

The win carries an immediate availability cost. Gregar Jenings is listed for six weeks, and Foo Warner for one. Tic Thorpe, Josh Alakazam and Tony Gyarzalez still have positive recovery counters. Those absences make the next assignment harder, even after Ftzpatrik’s efficient performance established a clear account of how the Reds won this one.

Saffron arrives after beating Lavender 38–9. Mt. Silver won their Week 15 meeting 36–33, and the conference final will require another answer to Archam Manning’s offense and a pass rush that just recorded seven sacks. Lynch gives the Reds a way to control possessions; the available receivers must again finish the difficult downs when the opponent creates them.

Blackthorn exits with a convincing road win at Cinnabar and a seven-point loss to the top seed. The Dragons led this game twice and had enough defensive recoveries to make the first half more profitable than it became. Mt. Silver made the second half its own through three successive touchdown drives, then forty-seven yards of closing offense. That sequence earns the Reds another week and gives the rest of our panel something specific to reconsider.
